qualification: Unauthenticated TLS-verified requests only, no account grant or credential, from the audited origin. A provider's answer to this origin is not a statement about any other origin or about authenticated access. Errors and 5xx do not establish provider CORS refusal, so they never produce a refusal here. Only providers with no compiled browser connection contract appear; every other provider's browser admission is in browser-policy.json.

kinds.built-in: This vault already does what the integration is for.
kinds.companion: Reached only through a native client or process (a command-line tool, the operating system, a device). A browser page cannot run it.
kinds.refuses-browser: The provider's own servers answer a request from the audited origin without admitting it. Needs a probe.
kinds.driver-pending: The provider's API answers the audited origin, so a browser connection is possible; OpenSesame has not built it. Needs a probe.
kinds.no-key-check: The provider answers the audited origin, but the only call the catalog names is public, so it cannot prove a key. Needs an unauthenticated-get probe that returned 200.

dispositions.summary: Bitwarden reads vault items through its command-line client. Its Vault Management API is the bw serve local server, which blocks any request that carries a browser Origin header unless it is started with --disable-origin-protection. Its cloud Public API manages organizations (members, collections, groups, events), not vault items, and Bitwarden's servers send no CORS headers to this site, so a page here cannot call it. Importing an export copies items into this vault as a local snapshot; it is not a live Bitwarden connection.

probes.note: Control: the same request from Bitwarden's own web vault origin is admitted, so the missing header above is an allow-list, not a probe failure.
Control: the same request from Bitwarden's own web vault origin is admitted.

alternative.label: Open Vault to import a supported export

dispositions.summary: Bitwarden Secrets Manager is used through its web app, its command-line client or its SDK. Its cloud servers send no CORS headers to this site, so a page here cannot call them.

Vaultwarden is a Bitwarden-compatible server, so vault items are reached the way Bitwarden's are: through a Bitwarden client that holds your master key, such as its command-line client. This catalog entry configures that client, which a browser page cannot run. Importing a Bitwarden-format export copies items into this vault as a local snapshot; it is not a live connection.

alternative.label: Open Vault to import a supported export

dispositions.summary: This catalog entry configures 1Password's command-line tool (op), which reads items on the computer it runs on. A browser page cannot run it. Importing an export copies items into this vault as a local snapshot; it is not a live 1Password connection.

dispositions.summary: The operating system's keychain can be read only by native code on the machine that owns it. A web page has no API for it.
pass keeps GPG-encrypted files in a directory on your computer, and this catalog entry points at that directory. A browser page cannot read a directory by path or run GPG.

sources.label: pass, the standard Unix password manager

dispositions.summary: This catalog entry points at a KeePass database file by path. A browser page cannot open a path, but it can open a file you choose: Vault → Import reads a KeePass database into this vault as a local snapshot.

alternative.label: Open Vault to import a supported export

dispositions.summary: This integration runs a command you name on the machine that holds the credential. A web page cannot start a process.

Tailscale device enrollment requires tailscaled and the OpenSesame native daemon, which a browser cannot run; a saved auth key alone would not enroll a device. Tailscale's management API also sends no CORS headers to this site.

Infisical Cloud's API answers browsers only on Infisical's own origin, so a page here cannot call it. A self-hosted Infisical can be configured to allow other origins, but OpenSesame has no Infisical connection contract yet.

The Proton Pass endpoint checked (pass.proton.me/api/pass/v1/user/access) answers a browser preflight from this site without CORS headers, so a page here cannot call it. Importing an export copies items into this vault as a local snapshot; it is not a live Proton Pass connection.

alternative.label: Open Vault to import a supported export

dispositions.summary: Plivo's API answers a browser preflight from this site without CORS headers, so a page here cannot call it.

AWS STS answers browser requests from this site (CORS allows any origin and the signing headers). Leasing credentials needs an IAM access key and AWS Signature Version 4 signing, which OpenSesame has not built for this service yet.

Azure App Configuration answers browser preflights from this site (CORS allows any origin). Calls need a store's access key or a Microsoft Entra token, and OpenSesame has not built that connection yet.

dispositions.summary: Google Cloud Secret Manager's API answers browser requests from this site. Calls need a Google access token, and OpenSesame has no way to obtain one here yet: its Google sign-in popup cannot run under this deployment's enforced cross-origin isolation.

Google Cloud's IAM Credentials API (the source of IAM credentials) answers browser requests from this site. Calls need a Google access token, and OpenSesame has no way to obtain one here yet: its Google sign-in popup cannot run under this deployment's enforced cross-origin isolation.

Let's Encrypt's ACME directory answers browser requests from this site, so a browser can create an account and an order. Finishing an order needs a DNS or HTTP challenge answered, which OpenSesame has not built.
This vault already seals every item with WebCrypto keys that never leave this device, so there is nothing to connect.
Your vault is a sealed local store: every item is encrypted on this device before it is written.
A passkey or security key can seal this vault, so a FIDO2 key needs no integration here.
This vault generates its own authenticator codes, so there is nothing to connect.
OpenSesame never keeps secrets in the clear on this device, so it offers no plain-text store.
